column1: # What a long Treasury DID across the equity drawdowns of the last 24 years, measured the way
# `uni.apps.MarketSim.measure` measures it: for every equity peak-to-trough decline of 15% or worse,
# the bond's LOG return over the same peak-to-trough span, in percent. The model's targets are the
# MEDIAN over these episodes, split by regime. `BondCrashSuite` / `bond_crash_tests` re-derive
# `bond growth-crash` and `bond infl-crash` from the rows below.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Both targets shipped through 0.21.0 as single-episode numbers -- +20.0%,
# which is 2008 alone and the LARGEST of the five growth-shock episodes here, and -25.0%, a rounding
# of the one inflation episode. The model computes a MEDIAN across episodes, so it was graded
# against a best case and read as understating a bond rally it in fact overstates. Same error class
# as `median depth %`: a named-episode statistic used where the model computes a distribution.
# THE SAMPLE IS SIX EPISODES and that is the honest limit of this anchor -- the growth median is a
# median of five. `-noise` prices that in: over 24-year histories the model produces growth-crash
# readings from about +2% to +28%, so one record barely pins it, and the target's weight is small
# for that reason rather than by choice.
# Equity SPY, bond TLT, daily Yahoo adjusted closes over their overlap, 2002-07-30..2026-08-03.
# TLT's effective duration is about 16-17 years against the model bond's 13.5, so a like-for-like
# 13.5-year anchor would be SMALLER still; the direction of the correction is not in doubt.
# regime: growth or inflation, by whether the decline is the 2022 inflation shock -- the model
#   splits on its own `inflPress` and this is the record's only inflation-regime drawdown.
peak
